title: Néron models of abelian varieties over a Dedekind domain
statement: Let $D$ be a Dedekind domain, $E=\operatorname{Frac}(D)$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $A/E$ be an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety]. There exist a smooth separated commutative $S$-group scheme $\mathcal A$ of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and an isomorphism $\mathcal A_E\simeq A$ making $\mathcal A$ a Néron lft-model of $A$. No excellence, completeness or residue-field perfection is assumed. A Dedekind domain here means a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one. A commutative group scheme has multiplication, inverse and identity morphisms satisfying the commutative group diagrams. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For a domain $D$ with fraction field $E$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$, a Néron lft-model of a smooth $E$-group $V$ means a smooth separated $S$-group $\mathcal V$, with an $E$-group isomorphism $\mathcal V_E\simeq V$ [def-pc-base-change], for which restriction is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_S(X,\mathcal V)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_E(X_E,V)$ for every smooth $S$-scheme $X$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Locally of finite type means that each affine source chart over an affine base chart has a finitely generated coordinate algebra [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; finite type additionally requires quasi-compactness.

source.place: BLR 1.3 Corollary 2, printed p.16, and 1.4 Theorem 3, printed p.19 (PDF pages 22 and 25), global existence; group structure as in 1.2 Proposition 6 and 10.1 after Definition 1 Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf.

proof.text: Fix a closed point $s$ of $S$. Its local ring $R=D_s$ is a DVR by [lem-sc-dedekind-localization-dvr]. Choose a geometric point over the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and its strict henselization $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ as constructed in [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]; [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dvr] gives a DVR, and put $L=\operatorname{Frac}(R^{\mathrm{sh}})$. By [lem-sc-abelian-variety-projective] choose a closed embedding $A\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_E$. For a point $[x_0:\cdots:x_n]\in A(L)$ choose an index $i$ where $v(x_i)$ is minimal among its nonzero coordinates. Then $v(x_j/x_i)\geq0$ for every $j$. The standard affine chart $A\cap\{x_i\ne0\}$ has coordinate algebra generated by the ratios $x_j/x_i$ modulo the equations of $A$. Assign each point to one minimizing index. These finitely many sets cover $A(L)$ and all their coordinate generators have valuation at least zero. Thus they satisfy exactly the boundedness hypothesis of [lem-sfb-bounded-group-local-neron-criterion], which gives a smooth separated finite-type $R$-model with the full mapping property. This argument uses no completeness or excellence of $R$.

source.place: BLR 1.1 Definition 2 and proof of Proposition 6 (projective case); 1.3 Theorem 1 and Corollary 2, printed pp.9-10,16

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-abelian-dense-open-spreading] to obtain a nonempty open $U\subseteq S$ and an abelian scheme $B/U$ with $B_E\simeq A$. By [lem-sfb-abelian-scheme-neron-property], $B$ has the full Néron mapping property over $U$. Properness includes separatedness and finite type, so $B$ has exactly the three geometric properties required of the open model in the patching lemma.

source.place: BLR 1.4 proof of Theorem 3, printed pp.19-20, and 1.2 Proposition 8, printed p.15

proof.text: The closed complement $S\setminus U$ contains no generic point. Since $D$ is a dimension-one domain, its nonzero prime ideals are maximal; hence every point of this complement is closed. The scheme $S$ is Noetherian, so [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-points-finite] makes the complement finite. For each point in it use the local model constructed in step 1. Apply [lem-sfb-neron-finite-complement-patching] with $V=A$ and open model $B$ from step 2. It produces a smooth separated finite-type $S$-scheme $\mathcal A$ with identified generic fibre $A$ and restriction bijections for all smooth $S$-schemes, including ones that are not quasi-compact. If the complement is empty the same lemma applies with no local models.

source.place: BLR 1.4 Proposition 1 and proof of Theorem 3, printed pp.18-20

proof.text: Extend $m_E:A\times_EA\to A$, $i_E:A\to A$ and $e_E:\operatorname{Spec}E\to A$ by the mapping property of step 3, using respectively the smooth test schemes $\mathcal A\times_S\mathcal A$, $\mathcal A$ and $S$. Finite products are smooth: on affine charts their structural rings are iterated tensor products, smooth by the base-change and composition clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition]; this is the affine-local smoothness criterion in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Each group identity compares two maps from a smooth finite product of $\mathcal A$ to $\mathcal A$ agreeing generically, so injectivity of the same restriction bijection proves it. The generic multiplication is commutative by [lem-sc-av-commutative]; apply injectivity with source $\mathcal A\times_S\mathcal A$ also to $m$ and $m\circ\mathrm{swap}$. This makes $\mathcal A$ a commutative $S$-group and the chosen generic identification a group isomorphism. Together with step 3 this is the required finite-type Néron lft-model.

source.place: BLR 1.2 Proposition 6, printed p.14 (PDF p.20); group identities follow directly from uniqueness in the mapping property

Give the projective-coordinate boundedness argument and extend all group operations by uniqueness; no assumptions added and no SGA used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NK-4402688f0 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, all 4 new nodes and every cited statement. BLR is not in literature/ (WANTED), so I checked against BLR 1.1/2, 1.2/8, 1.3/1 and 1.4/1,3 from knowledge of the book. Statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to the O4 snapshot. This is a first split, not a re-split. Step 1: D_s is a DVR (dedekind-localization-dvr); R^sh is a DVR (strict-henselization-dvr, applied to Spec R at its closed point). A ⊂ P^n_E, and taking the index i of minimal v(x_i) puts each L-point in the affine chart x_i≠0 with v(x_j/x_i)≥0, so the criterion's boundedness holds exactly with c_i=0. Step 2: the spreading node's output (smooth proper commutative group with connected fibres over a nonempty open U) is exactly the input of the abelian-scheme node; proper gives separated and finite type. Step 3: nonzero primes are maximal and S is Noetherian, so the complement is finite (noetherian-closed-points-finite). The local models over D_s from step 1 fit the patching node; r=0 is allowed. Step 4: m, i and e extend via the test schemes A×A, A and S (finite products smooth by base change and composition); group axioms and commutativity (av-commutative) follow from injectivity; elementary is justified. All new nodes are true, self-contained, statement-only, strictly smaller than the item, and none restates a clause of it. Duplicate search over the whole DAG (Néron, abelian scheme, spreading, boundedness) found only the semiabelian, torus and descent nodes, which are different results; weil-extension-to-abelian-variety works over a field only. Accepted tool_uses: dedekind-localization-dvr, strict-henselization-dvr, abelian-variety-projective, noetherian-closed-points-finite, smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition, av-commutative. Minor, no change made: the criterion calls R^sh a DVR without a citation (true by strict-henselization-dvr), and the patching node carries unused inline group-scheme definitions.

lean.statement: theorem exists_abelian_neron_model (D : Type u) [CommRing D] [IsDedekindDomain D] (hD : ringKrullDim D = 1) (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra D E] [IsFractionRing D E] (A : Over (Spec (.of E))) [GrpObj A] [IsAbelianVariety A] : ∃ G : Grp (Over (Spec (.of D))), IsCommMonObj G.X ∧ Smooth G.X.hom ∧ IsSeparated G.X.hom ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType G.X.hom ∧ QuasiCompact G.X.hom ∧ ∃ e : (Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap D E)))).mapGrp.obj G ≅ Grp.mk A, ∀ (X : Over (Spec (.of D))), Smooth X.hom → Function.Bijective (fun f : X ⟶ G.X ↦ (Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap D E)))).map f ≫ (Grp.forget (Over (Spec (.of E)))).map e.hom)
lean.note: The full Néron mapping property is stated inline using canonical Over.pullback. The generic-fibre identification is an isomorphism in Grp, hence respects the given group structures. IsDedekindDomain allows dimension zero, so hD retains the node’s explicit dimension-one convention.
